chunks: Zakat is upon nine things: upon wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, sheep, gold and silver.
and the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) pardoned what was apart from that.
It is not permissible to pay the zakat except to the people of walaya (allegiance to the Imams).
And from the people of walaya, zakat is not to be given to one's parents, one's child, one's husband, one's wife, one's slave, or anyone for whose upkeep the man is obliged.

key_terms.الزكاة: Zakat — the obligatory annual alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islamic practice
key_terms.النفقة: Nafaqa — obligatory financial maintenance/upkeep owed to certain family members
key_terms.الولاية: Walaya — spiritual and political allegiance/guardianship toward the Imams; here a condition for eligibility to receive zakat
key_terms.عفا: Pardoned/exempted — a prophetic dispensation, meaning no zakat is owed on goods not listed

ai.seo_question: What are the nine things upon which zakat is obligatory according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This legal ruling from Al-Amali al-Saduq specifies the nine categories of wealth subject to zakat (the obligatory alms-tax): four agricultural products (wheat, barley, dates, raisins), three livestock (camels, cattle, sheep), and two precious metals (gold and silver). The Messenger of God explicitly exempted all other goods. Critically, the text adds a distinctively Shia ruling: zakat may only be given to those who hold walaya (allegiance to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt), and even among them, one's dependents and financial obligations (parents, children, spouses, slaves) are excluded.

en.bilal-muhammad: Zakat is upon nine things: upon wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, sheep, gold and silver,
and the Messenger of Allah (s) pardoned what was apart from that.
It is not permissible to pay the zakat to anyone other than the people of walaya.
From the people of walaya it is not permissible to give to one’s parents, one’s child, one’s husband, one’s wife, one’s slave and anyone for whose expense the man is obliged.
